summary: Writes an array out as CSV text, quoting any cell that needs it.
description: To CSV turns an array into CSV text. Records become rows: leave Columns empty and every property found on the records is written, in the order they were first seen, or name the columns yourself to fix the order and drop the rest. An array of arrays — what Parse CSV produces with Has Header unticked — is written cell for cell with no header invented. The correctness of a CSV writer is entirely about quoting, and this one gets it right: any cell containing the delimiter, a quote or a newline is wrapped in quotes with its own quotes doubled, so the output reads back through Parse CSV unchanged. The record `id` the runtime mints is not written unless you name it in Columns, because it is not a column you put there.
whenToUse: Answering with a spreadsheet: a cloud function replying to an export request, a download button in a browser app, a file written to storage. Pair it with Parse CSV for 'read a supplier's file, filter it, send it back'.

ports.items: The array to write. Records become rows; an array of arrays is written cell for cell.
ports.columns: Which properties to write, in order, comma separated in one string. Empty means every property found, in first-seen order.
ports.delimiter: The character between cells. Any cell containing it is quoted automatically.
ports.includeHeader: Write the column names as the first row. Ignored for an array of arrays, which has no column names.
ports.count: How many data rows were written, not counting the header row.
ports.changed: Fires once CSV holds the freshly written text.

patterns: Query Records `items` → To CSV `items`; To CSV `text` → Response `pm-csv`: an export endpoint in three nodes.
Parse CSV → Array Filter → To CSV: read, narrow, write back. The round trip is exact, including cells containing commas, quotes and newlines.
antiPatterns: Building CSV by joining strings in an Expression or Function node. That is the quoting rule reimplemented, and it is wrong the first time a cell contains a comma.
Passing an array of arrays and expecting a header row. There are no column names to write; use records if you want one.
